chunks: From him, from Ali, from his father, from Safwan ibn Yahya, who said:
I asked Abu al-Hasan (peace be upon him) about a man who swears an oath while his inner intention is contrary to what he has sworn, and he said: 'The oath is based on the inner intention.'
ai.seo_question: How is an oath judged in Shia Islam when the spoken words differ from the inner intention?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam*, Imam al-Hassan al-Askari affirms that the legal validity of an oath depends on the speaker's inner intention (ضمير) rather than the literal semantics of the words, a principle crucial for resolving discrepancies in Shia jurisprudence. This ruling underscores the Shia emphasis on internal state (niyyah) as the primary determinant of legal acts, distinguishing it from schools that may prioritize the apparent meaning (zahir) of the utterance. It provides a foundational basis for understanding how oaths are categorized and fulfilled when the heart's intent diverges from the spoken phrase.
